analysis.title: Tech Implodes, French Bonds Blow Out, Nasdaq Hangs By A Thread
key_insights: NDX remains in the trading range in place since May, with 29k (futures) the make-or-break level. Tech volatility has surged while the index holds the range.
The VXN has taken out new recent highs while VIX trades below Friday's highs.
SOX is breaking below the trading range in place since May, apart from one brief overshoot and undershoot. The 200-day moving average sits slightly lower and momentum is extremely weak.
SMH volatility had been unusually depressed for weeks. VXSMH has now surged sharply higher.
Apple continues to defy the broader AI narrative. The relative AAPL vs NVDA trade outlined a few weeks ago continues to work, and Apple risks becoming the unintended winner of the AI unwind.
The OAT-Bund spread is at levels where conviction is hard to hold. TS Lombard has warned of further widening if budget negotiations fail to improve, with 200bp potentially in play.
The OAT-BTP spread continues to widen as France trades more like the European periphery. European banks are under heavy selling pressure, and the bearish SX7E view is maintained.
The euro has not yet reacted to the rise in the OAT-Bund spread. France remains largely a local problem for now but could become a wider European problem.
CSI 300 is at its most oversold level in the history of the data. The trend is bearish but the risk of a violent countertrend squeeze is growing.
Silver is trading around $55, described as the make-or-break level. Momentum is poor and a break lower could accelerate given little support below.

Managed Money sold $565 million in silver futures during October 6-13, the third consecutive week of selling. Cumulative selling is $2.2 billion, of which $160 million was long liquidation and $405 million fresh shorts.
